name: rsETH holder Safe (Uniswap v4 module) exploit, Yoink front-run
era: post-merge; mempool-dumpster covers the day but holds NONE of the attacker's, Yoink's or the second bot's txs (all private flow)
verdict_qualifier: mechanism is direct use of the ATTACKER'S OWN prepared executor contract (Yoink called its permissionless function), not a calldata copy; the attacker's finishing tx was never mined and is invisible (private), so the 'pre-empted a pending attacker tx' ordering is inferred from the attacker's own pattern in a later round and from nonce 4 being cancelled
verdict_reason: Attacker deployed executor 0x10605ee4 (block 25980523 idx 155) and called prepare() 0xd28cebb8 (tx 0x0a7d69ab, block 25980524 idx 207). Yoink tx 0x0e7680b0 (block 25980525 idx 0, one block later) called the executor's function 0x882d6bfa(2900e18,0,0) via its gen3 contract and received 2,899.99999 rsETH pulled out of the victim Safe's Aave position. A read-only eth_call of that same function from an arbitrary address reverts 'not prepared' at the state after block 25980523 and succeeds at the state after 25980524: the call only became possible once prepare() was mined. A second, unrelated searcher (0x492d2552, tx 0x16b9ddf9, idx 3) called the same executor function in the same block and its internal call reverted (already drained). In round 3 the same attacker did deploy (869) -> prepare (870) -> execute at idx 0 of the next block (871); in round 1 its finishing tx (nonce 4) never landed and the nonce was later burned by a self-transfer (blk 25980578). Yoink was therefore pre-empting the attacker's next-block finishing step.
protocol_loss_note: press (Blockaid/CoinTelegraph). The victim is an external rsETH holder's Gnosis Safe with an Aave v3 position, not Kelp's own contracts (Kelp: 'contracts are safe'). 2,900 aEthrsETH pulled; ~2,882.37 rsETH ended with Yoink's vault, 17.63 rsETH funded the swap that paid the builder.

auction.escalation: builder.ultrasound.money (0x94771940...): 13 bids at 2e-5-6e-5 ETH (16-31 txs, -6568..-4375 ms), 0.00018 ETH x4 (-3570..-2197), then 0.2066 ETH with 27 txs at -827 ms, 6.41 ETH at +157, 6.91 (+201), 8.17 (+213), 8.58 (+411), 9.34 (+578), 10.13 (+889), max visible 10.32 ETH (+897); the delivered block (13.862965 ETH, 27 txs) is on the ultrasound relay only, so its submission time is not published. Other builders reached the same level: Eureka 2.17 ETH at -306 ms (60 txs), up to 14.0033 ETH at +1416/+1469 (83 txs) via agnostic/flashbots; bombora 9.79 ETH at +822 -> 13.28 (+1050); Titan 9.91 ETH at +878 -> 13.85175 at +1638 (186-188 txs). Values of this size need the ~18.9 ETH Yoink payment in the block, so the bribe tx reached at least four builders (inferred; bid contents are not published).

reported_statements: CoinTelegraph 2026-09-15: Blockaid says attacker used a public keeper multicall to steer a custom Uniswap v4 liquidity module into an attacker-created hooked pool; Kelp paused the receiving address for 24 h and said Kelp contracts are safe.
Defiant/Unchained/Forklog: Yoink tx at position zero, original tx reverted (we find the finishing tx never landed; no reverted tx exists on the attacker EOA).
caveats: Ultrasound relay (which delivered the winning block) publishes no bids, so the winning block's submission time is unknown; time stamps of other builders' bids only bound it.
'First seen' is mempool-dumpster's; absence means private flow or a dumpster miss. Attacker, Yoink and the second bot all absent.
Whether Yoink saw the prepare tx in the block (public chain state) or in private order flow cannot be separated; the eth_call test shows only that it was needed.
Round 1 'nonce-4 stuck tx' is inferred from a burned nonce; its content is unknown.
Do not read the second bot as copycat evidence: it called the same executor but its identity/strategy is not analysed.
headline_text: One block after the attacker's prepare() tx, Yoink called the attacker's own executor and pulled 2,900 rsETH from a holder's Safe, paying a 18.93 ETH builder tip; 2,882.37 rsETH went back to a Safe signer about 30 hours later.

harmonized.verdict_reason: Yoink called the attacker's own prepared executor one block after prepare(); eth_call shows it reverts before prepare() and succeeds after; the attacker's finishing tx never landed.
harmonized.headline_note: Used the attacker's own prepared contract; ordering vs the attacker's finishing tx is inferred (that tx was private and never mined).
